Editorial inferences for Week 5 (chapter boundaries from official .srt cue times with the d70 offset removed; concept graph; topic order; corrections of numeric claims such as node sizes, labelled استنتاجی)

a.value: lecture5.srt cue times start near 01:00:00

b.value: The YouTube video starts at 0:00

discrepancies.note: Offset of exactly +01:00:00 subtracted before deriving chapter links (D39); all chapter times spot-checked against cue text.

discrepancies.topic: tree search fragment has no final return

a.value: search() ends with else if (number == tree->number) { return true; } and no return after the chain

b.value: gcc -Wall -Werror flags control reaching the end of a non-void function

discrepancies.note: Code kept verbatim; the Persian note explains that the last test is always true and a plain else would silence the warning.

a.value: list3.c and list4.c build the list but do not free it

b.value: valgrind with input 1 2 3 reports 48 bytes definitely/indirectly lost

discrepancies.note: Intermediate teaching versions; list9.c adds freeing. Noted in w05-n08.

a.value: 'First, node *list is declared, but it has a garbage value.'

b.value: list3.c declares node *list = NULL;

discrepancies.note: Prose describes an uninitialised declaration; the code initialises to NULL. Persian note says both.

a.value: 'We can print the list in the correct order as follows:' before list4.c

b.value: list4.c still prepends; input 1 2 3 prints 3 2 1

discrepancies.note: Persian note states the actual output (reversed).

a.value: 'we need 26 x 4 = 104 nodes just to store Toad!'

b.value: Lecture: four nodes, each an array of 26 pointers

discrepancies.note: Persian note: 4 nodes and 104 pointers.

a.value: 'Tries are always searchable in constant time.'

b.value: Lookup takes one step per letter, independent of the number of stored words; constant because word length is bounded

discrepancies.note: Persian note explains 'constant with respect to the number of words' (استنتاجی).

a.value: Hash table lookup in the worst case is O(n)

b.value: 'hopefully no bigger than N divided by K' ... 'Big O of N divided by K'

discrepancies.note: Both stated; Persian note explains that constants drop in big O, so n/k is still O(n).

a.value: Topics include 'Trees, Binary Search Trees'

b.value: Summing Up lists ADTs, stacks/queues, linked lists, hash tables and tries but not trees

discrepancies.note: Persian summary adds a sentence on trees, labelled.

discrepancies.topic: Stack: 'one place out of 5000' vs CAPACITY 50

a.value: 'You might imagine only using one place in the stack out of 5000.'

b.value: The stack code above uses const int CAPACITY = 50;

discrepancies.note: Persian note points out the mismatch.

a.value: queue has people[CAPACITY] and size only

b.value: Array-based queue also tracks front so dequeue need not shift elements

discrepancies.note: Both described in w05-n03; the short's version is labelled.

a.value: Trailing space after 'list = n;' in list8/list9; comment says 'link list' in list7

b.value: Style guide: no trailing whitespace

discrepancies.note: Kept verbatim on purpose; noted in w05-n09.

a.value: Alt text: '4 is at the top 3 and 5 are below that and 1 2 6 7 are below those'

b.value: Lecture and the BST rule put 2 and 6 under 4

discrepancies.note: The image itself (viewed on the build box) shows 4 at the root, 2 and 6 below, 1 3 5 7 as leaves, so only the alt text is wrong. Persian alt text describes the image; media.json keeps the official alt in alt_en_official.

a.value: 'It's probably going to be 12 because it's 4 for the int and 8 for the pointer'

b.value: sizeof(node) is 16 on x86-64 (4 bytes padding); valgrind shows 16-byte blocks

discrepancies.note: Persian note says 16 with padding (استنتاجی from the box measurement) and repeats 'use sizeof'.

a.value: 'so that's like 16, that's like 20 bytes' for an int and two pointers

b.value: sizeof is 24 on x86-64 because of alignment

discrepancies.note: Persian note says 24 (استنتاجی).

discrepancies.topic: 'A list in Python is indeed a linked list'

a.value: Lecture answer to a student question

b.value: CPython's list is a dynamic array of pointers, not a linked list

discrepancies.note: Persian note labels the correction استنتاجی; Python is Week 6.

a.value: 'you should use the internet to find hash functions ... cite your sources'

b.value: 'The hash function you write should ultimately be your own, not one you search for online.'

discrepancies.note: For Speller the pset rule governs; the guide and short page say so (D34).

a.value: '26 times 8 is probably 200 bytes'; 10 pointers 'on CS50 IDE, is 80 bytes'

b.value: 26 x 8 = 208; CS50 IDE was replaced by cs50.dev; shorts recorded 2017

discrepancies.note: Persian short page gives 208 and notes the dated environment.

discrepancies.topic: Lecture source files not in the notes

a.value: src5 contains list0-list9 (list5.c and list6.c included)

b.value: Notes show list0-list4 and list7-list9 only

discrepancies.note: list5/list6 inventoried, not reproduced.

a.value: random() returns 'a value between 0 and RAND_MAX, or 32767'

b.value: 32767 is the C minimum; glibc (cs50.dev) defines RAND_MAX as 2147483647

discrepancies.note: Irrelevant to % 2; guide notes it.

a.value: Refers to rules 'described in the background', but the page has no Background section; also 'see and see' typo

b.value: The rules are in Problem to Solve

discrepancies.note: Guide links Problem to Solve.

a.value: 'help50', 'pset5 directory', 'outting', 'more one way', links man.cs50.io

b.value: Folder is speller; CS50's manual is manual.cs50.io; help50 availability in today's cs50.dev not confirmed

discrepancies.note: Guide uses the folder name speller and flags help50 as possibly unavailable (استنتاجی).

discrepancies.topic: Anchor placement in the extracted Speller page

a.value: In the extracted copy the ids 'texts' and 'specification' sit one heading before their sections

b.value: The live page's #specification anchor is the Specification heading

discrepancies.topic: Trie: dated distribution and no check50

a.value: wget https://cdn.cs50.net/2022/fall/labs/5/trie.zip

b.value: 'No check50 for this one!'

discrepancies.note: Copied exactly as published.

discrepancies.topic: Section list.c has no NULL check

a.value: list.c uses malloc without checking for NULL

b.value: Kelly stresses checking malloc's return value

discrepancies.note: Code reproduced verbatim with a Persian caveat.

a.value: hash.c returns negative values for some inputs and uses a magic number 3

b.value: hash must return an index usable for table[N]

discrepancies.note: hash.c is link-only (D35); the caveat is in the section page.

discrepancies.topic: Chaining 'without ever running into the problem of collision'

a.value: '...into our hash table without ever running into the problem of collision'

b.value: Collisions still happen; chaining stores colliding values in a list

discrepancies.note: Persian short page: chaining handles collisions, it does not remove them (استنتاجی).

a.value: 'If you're using probing ... deletion is actually really easy'

b.value: Deleting from an open-addressing table needs care so later probes still find displaced entries

discrepancies.note: Persian short page labels the caveat استنتاجی.

a.value: Alt text of cs50Week5Slide084.png is identical to slide 77: 'n pointing to a new node with 2 as the number and null as the next'

b.value: The image (viewed on the build box) is captioned 'n->next = list;' and shows node 2 pointing to node 1 while list still points to node 1
